text: While every user strives to achieve maximum efficiency of their equipment, usually characterized by up-time or operational hours, different users have varying degrees of acceptance for lost efficiency in operations. A good example of these differences can be seen in discussions with experimental operators on specific beamlines at large facilities, where a large number of visiting scientists might operate the same beamline, leading to a high learning curve and lost experimental time at the beginning of an experimental period to tailor both software and workflows. When these machines are in operation, users expect single-button operation with the ability to run without focusing on the mechanics of operation (e.g. what gate charge voltage does an RF power supply require for optimal operation). Accelerators are seeing increasing use as substitutes for radioactive sources, with major government and private programs aimed at replacing radioactive sources with accelerator-based sources to mitigate several types of risk to safety, health, and the environment. The use of linear accelerators as X-ray sources has also helped popularize the development of commercially available, off-the-shelf units. 2.1.2 Government-Funded Accelerator Facilities The US Department of Energy (DOE) ecosystem of national labs and facilities is a complicated framework of interlocking jurisdictions and entities. For large-scale experimental facilities, there is an additional layer of complexity to determining responsibility due to a complicated web of funding sources and policy require- ments. Security and medical vendors are dominated by a small number of large manufacturers. ExamplesincludeIBA,ProTom,Varian(nowSiemens)formedicalapplications,aswellasAltairandLeidos for security applications. Smaller firms provide support infrastructure and equipment specialized for use in the particle accelerator market, such as Dimtel for particle beam monitoring and control. These private firms, due to the small size of the market and need to prevent losing business to their own customers (e.g. national labs, universities), often develop closed tooling and systems that require manufacturer support and maintenance to maintain a revenue stream while being able to support users.
